To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acceptance of human resources management processes and practices by individuals and the effectiveness of those processes and practices are moderated by both individual culture and organization culture.
the impact of human resource management (HRM) processes and practices on the acceptance and performance effectiveness of employees is moderated by both individual and organizational culture.

(a) the relationship between human resource management processes, such as training, and individual acceptance of those processes is moderated by both individual and organizational cultural values, and (b) individual and organizational cultural variables moderate the relationships between human resource management process and effectiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of cultural values, both individual and organizational, on the acceptance of human resources management policies and practices and on their effectiveness.
the effects of culture on (a) human resources management processes and practices, (b) the acceptability and effectiveness of such practices, and (c) the effectiveness of the organization.

the impact of cultural values and cultural diversity on (a) human resources management processes and practices, (b) their acceptance by individuals, and (c) the effectiveness of these processes and practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of human resource management practices and policies are moderated by the cultural diversity of the organization and the culture of the employee.
cultural values have a moderating effect on the acceptance and the effectiveness of human resource policies and practices.
culture has a significant impact on human resource management processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cultural values do moderate the relationship between human resource management processes, practices and the effectiveness of those processes and practices.
the more an individual’s values are consistent with the organizational culture, the greater the acceptance of human resources practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural context is important to consider in understanding the effectiveness of human resource practices.
the cultural values of the individuals and organizations involved are important factors to consider when implementing human resource management processes.
the impact of human resource management practices on acceptance and effectiveness is moderated by the cultural context in which they are embedded.
